narrow: The original two-sided conditional claim is false on the stated fixed-design class. A Gram lower bound makes the repaired local fit feasible but is not an optimal-recovery lower bound: an exact design can contain a point at the evaluation path, making the target estimable from its replicated mean, while the normalized Gram threshold is first crossed at a much larger bandwidth. For \(\lambda>1\), Gram coercivity also controls the squared local-polynomial weights but not their \(\ell_1\) norm; with unrestricted within-unit temporal dependence the conditional variance can exceed \(R_D\). The proposed claim preserves the proved positive conditional oracle upper bound and the treated and donor converses in the scalar-modulus regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), without assuming the missing sharpness property.
